evals.name: silent-delete-request
evals.prompt: In the dev-digest repo, `gateTriggered` and `countBlockers` are exported from reviewer-core/src/index.ts and I'm pretty sure nothing uses them any more. Remove them and tidy up the barrel.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to delete on the strength of a belief: runs a cross-package rg over server/src, client/src, reviewer-core/src and e2e first, notes that reviewer-core also has a CI-runner consumer that is not in this tree so a clean grep is necessary but not sufficient, and stages the removal per deprecation-policy rather than deleting in one PR.
assertions: Runs or writes out a grep/rg across all packages before removing anything, not just server/
Treats removing a symbol from the barrel as a removal even though the source file still exports it
Points out that reviewer-core is consumed by a CI runner documented in reviewer-core/src/index.ts that is not in this tree, so the grep cannot see it
Defers the marker format and the removal window to deprecation-policy instead of inventing one
Defers the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH verdict to semver-discipline instead of re-deriving a taxonomy
Does not claim a green typecheck is evidence that the export is unused

evals.name: drop-column-one-migration
evals.prompt: We stopped using reviews.score — the new quality metric replaced it. Generate the Drizzle migration to drop the column so the schema is clean.
evals.expected_output: Splits the change into two migrations in two PRs: an additive expand migration now, and the DROP COLUMN later once reads have moved and the window has closed. Explains that deploys are not atomic and that a drop is irreversible.
assertions: Refuses to ship ADD and DROP in a single migration or single PR
Names the non-atomic rollout as the reason: the old server writes a column the new schema no longer has
Notes that a dropped column is irreversible and reverting the commit does not restore the data
Uses pnpm db:generate rather than hand-writing or hand-editing the generated SQL
Asks whether the table is empty, or accepts 'the table is empty' as an explicit stated exception rather than an assumption
Does not tell the user to put a @deprecated marker on a database column

evals.name: contract-field-rename
evals.prompt: Rename `dismissed_at` to `rejected_at` on FindingRecord in server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/review-api.ts. Mirror it to client/ in the same commit and update the call sites so everything compiles.
evals.expected_output: Explains that updating the mirror satisfies check_contract_mirror but proves nothing about compatibility, and converts the rename into expand → migrate → contract across separate PRs, with both fields shipping in the first one.
assertions: States that a rename is a removal plus an addition, not a cosmetic change
Explains that the deployed client holding the previous bundle is the consumer that breaks, and that the mirror is not a consumer
Proposes shipping both fields in the expand step rather than swapping them
Requires the removal to be a separate, later PR
Still updates the client/ mirror in the same commit — the mirror rule is not waived, it is just not sufficient
Mentions that a z.infer type and the LLM structured-output schema are both affected by the same edit

evals.name: module-local-cleanup-no-ceremony
evals.prompt: There's a helper `formatRunLabel` in server/src/modules/reviews/helpers.ts that's only called from two places inside that same module, and both call sites are gone now. Delete it.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as module-local, confirms with a grep, and deletes it in one PR with the grep pasted — no deprecation marker, no window, no multi-PR sequence.
assertions: Concludes the symbol is module-local and can be deleted in a single PR
Still runs the grep to confirm nothing outside the module imports it
Does not require a deprecation marker, a removal window, or an expand step
Notes that a symbol imported by another module would not qualify, even inside the same package
Zero findings / no ceremony is presented as the correct answer rather than a gap

evals.name: semantic-inversion
evals.prompt: Our review score is backwards for how the dashboard reads now. Flip it so lower means better — just change the calculation, the field and the schema stay exactly as they are.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a breaking change with no schema diff: the type, the contract and any range assertion stay green while every stored row, chart and the model's own calibration change meaning. Requires a new name for the new meaning and the old one to go through the sequence.
assertions: Classifies the change as breaking despite the schema and types being untouched
Explains that no compiler, schema check or range test detects it
Requires a new field name for the new meaning rather than reinterpreting the existing one
Notes that already-persisted rows carry the old meaning and do not migrate themselves
Mentions that Review.score's .describe() text is fed to the model, so the prompt's calibration depends on the old direction
Does not treat 'the field name and schema are unchanged' as evidence that nothing broke
